_comment: Vacuous-test ratchet baselines (tkt-d88902f60f7c). `max` is a CEILING, not a target: the gate fails when a repo exceeds it, and it should only ever be revised DOWN. `path` is relative to the hardpack repo root and BINDS the row to a tree, so the ratchet cannot sweep one repo and report another's ceiling. `files`/`blocks` are read as a breadth floor, so a collapsed sweep fails instead of scoring a clean 0. `enforced` marks rows whose repo actually runs the check in a gate. Since the v0.19.0 distribution (tkt-05b1630bb53a) that means the repo's OWN CI running `ticket-workflow vacuous . --check` against its repo-local vacuous-baseline.json — hardpack alone enforces through THIS central file (its vitest self-check); the other enforced rows are cross-repo mirrors of their repo-local baselines, kept for the fleet view, and a drifted mirror misleads without failing anything. Rows carry an `accepted` list when their candidates were TRIAGED (tkt-7bac51ae3cc6): each entry is a candidate the audit read and accepted with the reason recorded. The RATCHET does not read these lists — it compares counts only, so a fixed accept plus a new candidate at the same count still passes; the lists serve the human re-triager (diff the sweep's candidates against them) and the ratchet test that pins accepted.length to max. A row without `accepted` is ceilinged-untriaged (deferred audit tier).
_regenerate: Do not hand-edit the counts. Run: node -e 'import("./scripts/probe/vacuous-tests.mjs").then(m=>{for(const [r,p] of Object.entries(require("./scripts/probe/vacuous-baseline.json").repos).map(([k,v])=>[k,v.path])){const s=m.sweep(p);console.log(r,s.files,s.blocks,s.candidates.length)}})' — the numbers below were generated that way, not transcribed.
_countsAreFloors: Counts are STILL FLOORS, not totals (tkt-9c818426feb3 narrowed the gap; the v0.19.0 packaged engine narrowed it again — it now sees destructured declarations, .forEach on a call result and for-await). These remain undetected: a collection declared in the enclosing describe/beforeEach or at module scope; two-level indirection (const b = a); reassignment (let xs = []; xs = compute()); and an out-param filled by a call (const rows = []; collect(rows)). Do not read a 0 as proof of clean.
_attribution: How the 08-11 numbers moved (tkt-9c818426feb3), measured by running the PRE-FIX probe against today trees so the two causes are separable. ticket-workflow 0 -> 6: only +1 is the fix, +5 are NEW vacuous tests added since 08-11 (its test files went 9 -> 17) and are tracked, not excused. equipment-schedule 19 -> 25: +4 fix, +2 new. copart-filter 4 -> 5: +1 fix. kanban stayed 0 because its one candidate was FIXED, not ceilinged (server/terminalAuth.test.ts asserted a container mount boundary entirely inside an unpinned loop). Raising a ceiling is a debt record, never an excuse: the split above is what says which part still needs fixing.
_lowered: 2026-08-16, tkt-898aaec13fb1: ticket-workflow 6 -> 0. The repo was re-swept before the fix and reported 8, not the 6 recorded here — two more had landed since (an audit control, and the byte-for-byte template drift check whose IDENTICAL list is matched by targetPath, so renaming an entry silenced it entirely). All eight are fixed upstream, each pin sitting outside its loop; see ticket-workflow#53. Breadth floors in every row below were regenerated in the same run, because a floor left behind is a collapsed sweep this ratchet would not notice. 2026-08-18, tkt-7bac51ae3cc6: equipment-schedule 25 -> 11 — the fresh sweep matched the recorded 25, triage fixed or rewrote down to 10 accepts (tkt-6a2232768981), then the critical-paths ticket's rebuilt replaceName sweep added 1 new accepted candidate, a probe false positive on a length-pinned call-derived collection (tkt-77046457a5df) — and copart-filter 5 -> 4: the re-sweep reported 6, not the recorded 5 (one had landed since), and 2 were fixed (tkt-98076f541a57). Every non-kanban `path` was also checked in this pass: the 08-17 projects/ consolidation moved kanban a level deeper, and four recorded paths silently pointed at nothing — the probe's refusing-to-sweep-nothing guard is what surfaced it rather than a clean 0.

_engine: Since 2026-08-18 (tkt-05b1630bb53a) the probe and the compare are the ticket-workflow package (pinned v0.19.0); vacuous-tests.mjs is a re-export shim and vacuous-ratchet.mjs keeps only the central-baseline layer (row paths, resolveRoot). The packaged engine detects shapes the old one missed (destructured loop sources, forEach on a call result, for-await) and excludes it.todo from block counts, so breadths were regenerated in this pass on clean mains — EXCEPT equipment-schedule, whose tree was mid-flight on another session’s branch; its recorded breadth is still the 08-18 pre-swap sweep, and the packaged engine read 15 candidates against its ceiling of 11 on that dirty snapshot. Re-triage belongs to its adoption pass, on a clean main.
_enforcedProbe: `enforced` records mutable external state (another repo's CI wiring), verified 2026-08-18 — re-verify, never trust: in the repo, `gh workflow list --all` must show its gate workflow active AND its gate must reach `ticket-workflow vacuous . --check` (grep the workflow/verify chain for `vacuous`; ticket-workflow instead self-checks via src/vacuous/ratchet.test.ts "this repo against its own ceiling"). A disabled workflow contributes NO check and everything reads green — the exact rot this repo's own review workflow demonstrated.
